JUDGMENT :(per Mr. Man oj Ku m ar Gu p t a, C.J.)
1. The present writ petition has been filed
challenging stipulation regarding the experience in the
Notice I nviting Bid, which lays down that the bidder should
have experience of sim ilar contracts having MAF
(Manufacture Authorization Form ) of HAMS Software in the
role of contractor for at least last 05 years prior to the bid
subm ission deadline. The contract is for autom ation work
at autom ated driving test track in District Alm ora,
Uttarakhand.
2. The petitioner- firm is stated to have subm itted
its bid and now apprehending that it would not be
considered as it does not have the said experience, has filed
the writ petition challenging the condition above in Clause
1

2026:UHC:1982-DB
2.2(A)(b), which is as : -
"A. Qu alif icat io n Cr it er ia:
a) .......
b) The Bidder should have Experience of sim ilar contracts having
MAF (Manufacture Authorization Form ) of HAMS Software in the role
of contractor for at least the last [ 5)} years prior to the bid
subm ission deadline."
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner subm itted
that the said condition am ounts to a restrictive trade
practice, as the experience needed in a particular software
would restrict the persons eligible for the contract. He
subm its that it is an open source software of Microsoft and
Maruti Suzuki and, indirectly, it would result in extending
benefit to these com panies to the exclusion of other
com panies having sim ilar software and also entities who are
using other sim ilar software.
4. I t is settled that an authority who invites a
tender or auction bid is entitled to set out the term s and
conditions, which suit its needs and requirem ents of the
work to be perform ed under the contract. Since the
autom ation work has to be carried out using the software
afore-said, which the respondents felt is suitable for
m eeting their needs and requirem ents, therefore, the
petitioner cannot com e forward challenging the said
stipulation.
5. We are of the considered opinion that the
2

challenge is wholly baseless and, accordingly, the writ
petition is dism issed.
6. Pending application, if any, also stands disposed
of.
 MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA, C.J.
